title: TechnicalQaReport
description: The technical QA verdict on one Render (PRD REQ-100/084/104/106, tech-spec §15 step 7). Wired as a HARD GATE: no render reaches review or packaging without one, and a missing or malformed report fails closed. Two structural commitments carry the honesty: (1) `checksRun` is a ledger of EVERY check in the closed enum with its status and, for anything not run, a required reason — so 'nothing was found' can never be confused with 'nothing was looked at'; (2) `gateStatus` is COMPUTED from findings and waivers by deterministic code, never authored — a report claiming `pass` beside an unwaived blocker is a contradiction the resolver rejects.

changelog.reason: Initial v1 (Phase 4, task 8; D-35 gate statuses; D-37 deterministic blockers). Findings carry an OPTIONAL time range but a REQUIRED `fix` string: REQ-106 asks for actionable reports, and a finding a reviewer cannot act on is noise no matter how precisely it is timestamped.

Added required `waivedFindingIds`. The first cut recorded only `waiverIds`, so nothing downstream could tell WHICH findings a waiver covered — and the runner gate that tried to compute it compared a finding id against a list of waiver ids, a predicate that is always false. Recording the covered finding ids makes `pass_with_waivers` verifiable from the report instead of merely asserted by it.
Added required `planHash` so a waiver's scope is checkable from the report alone (see qa-waiver-v1 same-date entry).

rulesetVersion.description: The `technical-qa-v1.yaml` ruleset version these thresholds came from (tech-spec §12.1). Thresholds are DATA: changing a number changes behaviour with no code change, and this field is what makes a past verdict re-interpretable against the numbers that actually produced it.

gateStatus.description: D-35. `pass` = no findings above info. `pass_with_waivers` = every warning is covered by a valid waiver and there are no blockers. `fail` = at least one blocker, or an uncovered warning. Blockers are NON-WAIVABLE, so no waiver can move a report out of `fail`.

checksRun.description: One entry per check in the closed enum — including the ones that did not run. The Phase 2 lesson this encodes: a sub-stage that omitted a whole modality without recording it made an honest pipeline dishonest one layer up.

status.description: `skipped` is a deliberate non-applicability (a silence check on an audio-less render); `errored` is a check that tried and failed. Collapsing them would let a broken detector present as an inapplicable one.

reason.description: Null ONLY when status is `ran`. Anything else requires a reason; the resolver enforces it (tech-spec §3 forbids if/then/else).

findings.description: Every problem found, most severe first. Empty is a legitimate result — and is distinguishable from 'not checked' only because `checksRun` exists.

findingId.description: Deterministically derived from (checkId, object, time range) so re-running QA over the SAME render yields the SAME ids — which is what makes a waiver referencing them meaningful.

severity.description: `blocker` is non-waivable by construction (D-35); `warning` may be waived by a named human; `info` never affects the gate.

waivable.description: Restated alongside severity so a waiver validator never has to re-derive the policy. The gate asserts `waivable === (severity !== 'blocker')`; a finding that disagrees with itself is rejected rather than resolved in either direction.

object.description: What the finding is about — REQ-106's 'object': a clip id, a caption cue index, `output`, or an audio track.

message.description: What is wrong, stated as an observation with the measured value and the threshold it breached.

fix.description: REQ-106: what to do about it. Required — an unactionable finding trains people to skim the report.

timeRange.description: Where in the OUTPUT timeline (REQ-106 'time range'), or null for a whole-file finding such as wrong dimensions. Exact ticks, never float seconds (tech-spec §3).

waiverIds.description: The QaWaiver records consulted when computing `gateStatus`. Recorded even when empty, so 'this passed cleanly' and 'this passed because someone waived two warnings' are distinguishable from the report alone.

waivedFindingIds.description: The FINDING ids those waivers cover — deliberately separate from `waiverIds`, which are the waivers' own identities. Without this a reader of the report cannot tell WHICH warnings were accepted, and any attempt to re-derive `gateStatus` from the report alone has to compare a finding id against a waiver id, which is always false. Recorded so a downstream gate can verify `pass_with_waivers` rather than trust it.

planHash.description: The render plan these findings were produced against. A QaWaiver names the same value; the gate accepts a waiver only when the two agree, which is what stops an acceptance from carrying across an edited plan.
